title: Account True ROAS slipped below breakeven to 0.98 (from 1.17); online-order revenue fell 30% while spend fell only 17%
detail: Real GA4 web-purchase revenue dropped $10,445 -> $7,309 (-30%, -$3,135) while spend was cut just $8,929 -> $7,431 (-17%). Because tracked revenue fell almost twice as fast as spend, True ROAS crossed under 1.0 to 0.98 — the account no longer covers its ad cost on tracked online orders alone. Blended ROAS (3.49 vs 3.79) understates this. The standing caveat holds: in-store lift from these local campaigns is not captured here, so 0.98 is the measurable floor, not the full return. But the trend is the concern — this is the second straight period of decline. Recommended: run the deliberate 4-week spend-reduction test in 2-3 markets (watch Toast same-store sales) to isolate the in-store value the online number can't see, before this erodes further.

title: Budget misallocation WORSENED: Milwaukee took +$114 to become the #1 spender ($1,127) at True ROAS 0.82, while best-performer Whitefish Bay was cut again to $557
detail: Last week flagged Milwaukee as over-funded relative to its True ROAS; instead of correcting, its spend rose $114 and it is now the single largest spender at $1,127 — yet its True ROAS is 0.82 (2nd-worst among funded stores) and it produced $919 in online orders. Whitefish Bay, the BEST True ROAS at 1.68, was cut $340 to $557 and still generated MORE order revenue ($935) than Milwaukee on half the spend. Middleton (True ROAS 1.20, improved) was also cut $532. The reallocation went exactly the wrong way. Concrete action: shift ~$300-400/period out of Milwaukee into Whitefish Bay and Middleton (raise their budget caps / target ROAS) — same spend, more measurable order revenue.

title: Sun Prairie True ROAS stuck at 0.83 for a second straight period (baseline 1.45) — no recovery, orders down to 15
detail: Flagged last week when it collapsed; it did NOT recover. True ROAS 0.83 (prev-period 1.45), the largest drop again this window (-0.62), on spend that was itself cut $856 -> $556. Online orders fell to 14.9 ($462 revenue) — the lowest of any Madison-area store. Blended ROAS barely moved (3.90 vs 4.03), so only the True ROAS view catches it. Two periods low rules out a one-week blip: check the Sun Prairie online-ordering funnel end-to-end (Toast confirmation page / GA4 purchase tag still firing?) — a tracking break produces this exact signature. If tracking is intact, the store's online demand has genuinely softened and budget should follow.

title: Top Locations campaign grew to $391 at True ROAS 0.32 instead of being paused — still the account's worst and cannibalizing store campaigns
detail: Recommended for pause last week when it was spinning up (~$214); it instead grew to $391 with True ROAS 0.32 and just 5.9 online orders ($124). It overlaps geographically with the per-store PMax campaigns, so it is both the least efficient campaign and diverting impressions/budget/data away from the store-level campaigns that convert better. Action: pause PMax_Cube_Top Locations and let budget flow back to store campaigns — the data now confirms it two periods running.

title: Champaign chronically below 0.50 True ROAS (0.42) for a third period — consistently unprofitable on orders
detail: Champaign True ROAS 0.42 (prev 0.47, ~0.45 the period before): $413 spend for $174 of online-order revenue (9 orders). Unlike stores that at least break even, this one is persistently the worst funded store and not improving. Likely causes to rule out: (1) online ordering isn't well set up/promoted for Champaign, or (2) it's an out-of-market college store where local-visit value doesn't convert online. Recommend halving its budget and reallocating, or confirming the ordering funnel works before continuing to fund it at this level.

title: Meta efficient as traffic (cost/LPV improved to $0.35) but still no purchase tracking — the remaining blind spot
detail: Meta spend $650 (-$43) delivered 1,839 landing-page views at $0.35/LPV, an improvement from $0.41 — solid as a traffic buy. New this period: 'falafel launch 0706' ($131) and 'brookfield sales 0726' ($4, barely started); 'Berry Good Summer Salad' wound down to $44. But all six campaigns remain traffic-objective with no purchase event, so this $650/period can't report True ROAS the way Google now does. Add the Meta Pixel purchase event on the Toast order-confirmation page to close the gap, and migrate off the legacy personal-named ad account (act_35967094) to the business account.
